title: Xu
capsule: Xu (徐) was an ancient state of eastern China in the Huai River valley, straddling what is now northern Jiangsu and Anhui, traditionally linked to the Huaiyi peoples and a longstanding rival of the Zhou royal house. During the Western Zhou it intermittently led coalitions of Huai River peoples against Zhou hegemony, and bronze inscriptions record campaigns against it, including the well-known expedition attributed to King Mu. Worn down over generations by the expanding southern power of Chu, Xu was finally extinguished in 512 BCE by the state of Wu: King Helü's forces are said to have flooded the Xu capital, after which its last ruler, Zhangyu, surrendered and fled into exile in Chu.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Xu's territorial extent is poorly attested; its boundaries are reconstructed from Zhou bronze inscriptions and later Han histories with limited geographic precision.
